title: throughput-solarization-notebook-jules
content:
Goal: quick exploration of 'solarization' arrival pattern -> periodic modulation of QPS to probe resonance in batching/eviction/coldpath. Idea: inject a slow sine-like QPS envelope on top of baseline to see throughput harmonics and tail amplification.

Setup
- Cluster: dev-dedicated-pool (4x A100 equivalent), model: llama-7b-quant-int8 (v2.3.1), sequence len avg=256 (prompt+resp).
- Worker config: batch_ms=12, max_batch_tokens=2048, idle_kv_ttl=30s.
- Load tool: wrk2 w/ custom driver script (sinusoidal qps scheduler). Command snippet: 
  ./wrk -t4 -c200 -d120s --script=sine_qps.lua http://10.0.8.12:8080/generate

Observations (raw)
- Baseline steady QPS 120 => p50=48ms, p95=112ms, p99=248ms, GPU util ~62%
- Sine amplitude +/-60 around base 120 (range 60–180), period = 40s -> notable 2nd harmonic in throughput: burst peaks saturate at 180QPS but tail jumps.

Selected samples (period snapshots):
T=phase0 (rising): QPS=80 => p50=42ms p95=98ms p99=210ms
T=peak: QPS=180 => p50=76ms p95=220ms p99=780ms (spike clusters)
T=falling: QPS=100 => p50=46ms p95=120ms p99=260ms

Quick hypothesis notes
- Batching coalescence hits a sweet spot near 120 QPS; above ~150 QPS we see queues spill to coldpath and KV eviction thrash (idle_kv_ttl=30s might be too short).
- 2nd harmonic suggests request alignment with internal batching window (12ms) causing intermittent larger micro-batches -> latency tail.
- GC/pthread wakeups on host observed at peaks (dmesg spikes), kernel scheduling may add jitter.

Telemetry snippets (from metrics ingest)
- avg_batch_size: baseline 9.1 -> peak 14.7
- kv_cache_hit: baseline 0.87 -> peak-phase 0.63 (evictions)
- gpu_mem_pressure: 71% -> 93% at peak

Quick ASCII heatmap (p99 over time, one period):
[60] ---***---------*******-----**********----
(legend: more * = worse latency)

Mini experiments to run next (ordered)
1) Increase idle_kv_ttl -> 120s, re-run same sine envelope. Expect fewer evictions and lower p99 at peaks.
2) Decrease batch_ms to 8ms (risk: smaller throughput), test whether harmonic shifts.
3) Add backpressure smoothing on ingress (token-bucket smoothing, tau=5s) to remove sharp slope on rising edge.
4) Swap to q4_0 model variant to see GPU mem impact.

Notes-to-self
- Save full traces t=2026-02-27-peakA (profiling folder).
- Plot heatmaps of batch size vs p99 over many periods. Want to identify stable operating band and resonance frequencies.
- Raise ticket referencing PROJ-3421 if we confirm KV ttl fixes tail.

Loose conclusions so far
- Periodic modulation (solarization) surfaces hidden resonances in batching+cache layers not obvious with steady-state tests.
- Short KV TTL + bursty leading edges => eviction thrash -> p99 explosions.
- Operational mitigation: longer KV TTL + ingress smoothing + smaller batch_ms seems promising.
